q: Instructions that supplement or modify drawings, specs, & general conditions of the contract.
n: Per the MST answer key: Special provisions.

q: Which printed document sets out the procedural and administrative terms of the contract?
n: General conditions.

q: Guarantee the quality of materials and workmanship performed.
n: Per the MST answer key: Guarantee bond.

q: What is a preset sum the contractor pays for delays?
n: Agreed in advance.

q: Letter needed for demolition.
n: Per the MST answer key: Letter of intent.

q: 1st step for building permit processing.
n: Per the MST answer key: Barangay clearance.

q: 2nd step for building permit processing.
n: Per the MST answer key: Locational.

q: 3rd step for building permit processing.
n: Per the MST answer key: Zoning.

q: 4th step for building permit processing.
n: Per the MST answer key: Application of building permit.

q: Responsible for the issuance of electrical permits.
n: Per the MST answer key: City hall.

q: Whatcolor is the envelope for commercial projects?
n: Per the MST answer key: Red.

q: What color is the envelope for residential projects?
n: Per the MST answer key: Yellow.

q: What color is the envelope for industrial projects?
n: Per the MST answer key: Violet.

q: Whatcolor is the envelope for institutional projects?
n: Per the MST answer key: Blue.

q: Which does NOT go on the cover sheet of an architectural set?
n: The roof plan is a regular sheet.

q: What security does the contractor post to guarantee the work will be done per the contract?
n: It protects the owner against default.

q: The amount retained by the owner shall be released how many months after the date of the final payment?
n: Per the MST answer key: 3months.

q: How many months is the retention period where the contractor should address defects after turnover of construction?
n: Per the MST answer key: 2months.

q: In preparation of the contract documents, the architect should always consider and include in the contract the following provisions except one:
n: Per the MST answer key: Out of court settlement.

q: In labor-materials ratio, what is the most common ratio used in the Philippine setting in coming up with an estimate?
n: Per the MST answer key: 70-30%.

q: What is to be secured first before excavation for a basement?
n: Per the MST answer key: Excavation permit.

q: Who checks the accuracy of a subcontractor's shop drawings before they go to the architect?
n: The general contractor reviews first.

q: Which of these is NOT an ancillary permit?
n: Fencing is an accessory permit.

q: If the builder doesn't own the lot, what must he submit for a building permit?
n: Plus a copy of the title.

q: A written statement from the architect confirming the amount due to the contractor for work accomplished.
n: Per the MST answer key: Certificate of completion.

q: Which of these cannot issue a construction (surety) bond?
n: Bail bonds are for criminal cases.

q: Which is NOT signed and sealed by the architect?
n: Per the MST answer key: Roof plan.

q: What makes a building permit void?
o: Work not started within a year of issuance
Work stopped for a year for lack of funds
n: PD 1096 Sec. 207 (work suspended 120 days also voids it).

q: "Bid" and ______ mean the same.
n: A tender is a bid.

q: How is design-build commonly rendered?
n: Design-build by administration or by guaranteed maximum cost.

q: A horizontal cut about 1.2 m above the floor, looking down at walls and fixtures, is a:
n: The floor plan.

q: Which body acts on zoning exceptions, reclassification or changes to the zoning ordinance?
n: The local legislature amends ordinances.

q: What is a fully signed offer to do the work the project calls for?
n: Per the MST answer key: Contract.

q: Who issues building permits in an LGU?
n: The Office of the Building Official.
